feature: Typing / in Ask lists the commands you can run
summary: Ask's field is now also the command list: type / and every menu command is there by name, filtered as you type, and Return runs it. After you ask, the conversation stays on screen in a dock at the window's left instead of vanishing.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open any picture with a layer on it. Walks: ask-slash-lists-commands-walk, ask-stays-up-after-asking-walk, ask-narrow-window-has-no-dock-walk.

try.do: Pick a layer, press Command K and type /.
try.shotNote: This picture shows the window behind another app, so blue buttons and picked controls can read grey.

try.do: Type duplic. The list narrows to Duplicate Layer.
try.shotNote: This picture shows the window behind another app, so blue buttons and picked controls can read grey.

try.do: Press Return. The layer is copied, the composer goes, and Duplicate Layer is a row in the Agent group.
try.shotNote: This picture shows the window behind another app, so blue buttons and picked controls can read grey.

try.do: Press Command Z. One press takes the copy back.
Press Command K, type add a blue rectangle, press Return. The dock opens at the left with your words and what it is doing.
try.shotNote: This picture shows the window behind another app, so blue buttons and picked controls can read grey.

try.do: When it finishes, click the row in the Agent group. The rectangle is picked on the canvas and in Layers.
try.shotNote: This picture shows the window behind another app, so blue buttons and picked controls can read grey.

try.do: Press Command K. The same conversation floats back over the canvas; Escape returns it to the dock.
try.shotNote: This picture shows the window behind another app, so blue buttons and picked controls can read grey.

try.do: Click the X on the dock. The canvas takes the room back and the Agent group's field returns.

evaluate: Is 300 points at the left the right price for keeping the conversation up, or should the dock close by itself when a request finishes?
Should a command you run from / get a row in the Agent group, or do only requests belong there?
On a picture, are the dimmed commands that cannot run now useful under the list, or just noise?
Does a row per choice (Align Left, Speed 50%) read well, or would you rather pick the command and then the choice?
rough: The canvas zoom changes as the dock comes and goes, because the picture refits the narrower column, so the picture jumps a little when Command K floats the conversation back.

The mock's line "Ask for a change, or type / for a command" is 41 characters, over the chrome's 30: the field says "Ask, or type / for a command" and the mock's whole line is the field's hover tip (UX-PATTERNS §4).
The mock's "No command matches." is a no-X placeholder and a sentence: the list says Nothing matches (UX-PATTERNS §4).

The mock's New conversation button is left out of the chat header, and the chat shows the latest request rather than the whole transcript. Task ask-chat-has-the-mock-s-new-conversation-button covers both.

The mock's rows carry an icon for each command. The app's command table has none, so a row shows the icon of its area (layers, timeline, view). Task ask-chat-has-the-mock-s-new-conversation-button covers it.
A few commands are not in the list because they need a value no row can hold: a length, a word, or a name from this document. They stay in their menus.
Below 900 points of window there is no dock, and the Agent group alone says how a request is going.
Toggle commands in the list do not show their tick.
